questions.stem: How many Schedules does the Indian Constitution contain as of the latest amendment, and which Amendment added the most recent one?

options.option_text: 10 Schedules; the 10th added by the 52nd Amendment (1985)
12 Schedules; the 12th added by the 74th Amendment (1992)
11 Schedules; the 11th added by the 73rd Amendment (1992)
12 Schedules; the 12th added by the 86th Amendment (2002)

questions.explanation: The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules. The 9th Schedule was added by the 1st Amendment (1951), the 10th by the 52nd Amendment (1985, anti-defection law), the 11th by the 73rd Amendment (1992, Panchayats), and the 12th — the most recent — by the 74th Amendment (1992, Municipalities). Option C confuses the 11th and 12th; option A stops short; option D cites the wrong amendment year.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution distributes legislative subjects between the Union and the States, and how many lists does it contain?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule allocates legislative subjects across THREE lists: Union List (currently 97 subjects), State List (currently 59 subjects), and Concurrent List (52 subjects). The Sixth Schedule deals with tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram — unrelated. The Concurrent List was retained in the 1950 Constitution, so option C is wrong. The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects of Panchayats, not Union-State distribution.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution is commonly referred to as the:
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule, inserted by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985, contains provisions relating to disqualification of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on grounds of defection — hence the nickname 'Anti-Defection Law'. Language matters are in the Eighth Schedule; Panchayats are in the Eleventh; Union-State distribution is in the Seventh.

questions.stem: How many languages are currently recognised in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, and which Amendment last added four languages — Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali?
questions.explanation: Original Eighth Schedule had 14 languages. The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi (→ 15). The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali (→ 18). The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, taking the total to 22. Option A conflates the amendments; option D overstates the current count.

questions.stem:
Match the Schedule with its subject and select the correct pairing:
(i) Second Schedule — Salaries and emoluments of constitutional officials
(ii) Third Schedule — Oath forms for officeholders
(iii) Ninth Schedule — Acts protected from judicial review
(iv) Sixth Schedule — Centre-State distribution of powers
questions.explanation: Pairings (i), (ii) and (iii) are CORRECT. The Second Schedule lists salaries/emoluments of the President, Governors, Speakers, Judges etc. The Third Schedule contains the oath/affirmation forms. The Ninth Schedule (added by 1st Amendment) shields laws from judicial review — though Kesavananda Bharati and I.R. Coelho limit this. Pairing (iv) is WRONG: Centre-State distribution is in the SEVENTH Schedule, not the Sixth. The Sixth deals with tribal areas in north-eastern states.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Parts of the Indian Constitution is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Part IV contains Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36–51)
Part IV-A — Fundamental Duties — was inserted by the 44th Amendment
Part IX-A dealing with Municipalities was added by the 74th Amendment

questions.explanation: Statement C is INCORRECT. Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A) were inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendations, NOT the 44th Amendment (the 44th, 1978, restored several pre-Emergency safeguards but didn't add FDs). All other statements are correct: Part III covers FRs, Part IV covers DPSP, and Part IX-A (Municipalities) was inserted by the 74th Amendment (1992) alongside Part IX (Panchayats) via the 73rd.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of:

options.option_text: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states OTHER than the north-eastern states covered by the Sixth Schedule
Tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
Panchayati Raj Institutions across all states

questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule provides for the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states OTHER THAN Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram — the latter four are governed by the Sixth Schedule's autonomous-district-council model. States covered by the Fifth Schedule include Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan and Telangana. Option B describes the Sixth Schedule, option C describes the Eleventh, option D describes the Second.

questions.stem: Which Schedule originally contained provisions concerning the territories of the Indian Union, and what did the 7th Amendment (1956) change about it?

options.option_text: The First Schedule; the 7th Amendment reorganised states on linguistic lines into Part A, B, C, D states
The First Schedule; the 7th Amendment abolished the Part A/B/C/D classification and created the present States and Union Territories listing
The Fourth Schedule; the 7th Amendment re-allocated Rajya Sabha seats
The Second Schedule; the 7th Amendment changed salaries of governors

questions.explanation: The First Schedule contains the names of States and Union Territories of India along with their territorial extent. Pre-1956, the Constitution classified states into Part A (former governors' provinces), Part B (former princely states), Part C (chief-commissioner provinces) and Part D (other territories). The 7th Amendment Act 1956 — following the States Reorganisation Act — abolished this A/B/C/D classification and reorganised India into 14 States and 6 Union Territories (the current structure has since evolved to 28 States + 8 UTs). Option A describes the pre-1956 layout but mis-attributes the change. Options C and D describe different Schedules.
questions.subject: Polity
